# Design Journal

### Date: 28/07/2026

---

## Section 1 — Specific Bugs

### Bug 1

**Issue:** The initial HTML parser extracted raw text from the document but did not correctly ignore HTML comments, causing unnecessary content to appear in the extracted output.

**Observation:** Comment detection was added to the parser, allowing comment blocks to be skipped completely while continuing normal parsing for visible page content.

---

### Bug 2

**Issue:** Consecutive whitespace characters generated by HTML formatting resulted in irregular spacing in the extracted text, reducing the quality of the indexed content.

**Observation:** A whitespace normalization mechanism was implemented to collapse multiple whitespace characters into a single space while preserving readability.

---

### Bug 3

**Issue:** Certain nested HTML elements caused portions of visible text to be skipped because tag transitions were not handled consistently.

**Observation:** The parsing logic was refined to correctly resume text extraction after nested tags, ensuring that all visible content was preserved.

---

## Section 2 — Failed Attempts

### Attempt 1 — Removing HTML Tags

Initially, HTML tags were removed by simply ignoring everything between `<` and `>`. Although this removed markup successfully, it failed to handle HTML comments correctly and occasionally produced unwanted output.

The parser was redesigned to explicitly detect comments separately from normal tags, resulting in more accurate text extraction.

---

### Attempt 2 — Whitespace Handling

The first implementation directly appended every visible character to the output string. While functional, it preserved excessive whitespace introduced by HTML formatting.

Instead of storing every whitespace character, the parser now appends only a single space between consecutive text segments, producing cleaner output for indexing.

---

### Attempt 3 — Parsing Nested Elements

The original parsing logic worked well for simple HTML documents but occasionally missed visible text when multiple nested tags appeared close together.

The parsing algorithm was refined to carefully manage transitions between text and markup, allowing nested elements to be processed without losing surrounding content.

---

## Section 3 — Design Decisions

Today's work focused on improving the accuracy and reliability of HTML text extraction for the indexing module.

The following design decisions were finalized:

* Implemented explicit detection and removal of HTML comments.
* Improved handling of nested HTML tags.
* Added whitespace normalization during text extraction.
* Preserved only visible text while ignoring HTML markup.
* Validated parser behavior using multiple HTML samples.
* Cleaned the parser implementation for readability and maintainability.
* Prepared the parser for integration with the inverted index module.

These design decisions improve the quality of extracted text and provide cleaner input for subsequent indexing operations.

## Section 5 — Learning Reflection

Today's work emphasized that accurate preprocessing is fundamental to building a reliable search engine. Even small inconsistencies in HTML parsing, such as improper comment handling or excessive whitespace, can negatively affect the quality of the generated index.

Refining the parser also demonstrated the importance of designing algorithms that correctly handle real-world HTML rather than only well-structured documents. By improving comment detection, nested tag handling, and whitespace normalization, the parser now produces cleaner and more meaningful text, providing a stronger foundation for the indexing pipeline.
